name: RudyQ Shield
author: Rudolph DSouza

sections.description:
RudyQ Shield is a privacy-first, self-hosted CAPTCHA designed for real humans.

Instead of classic math problems like “1 + 1 = ?”, it asks natural language number questions in the 0–9 range, for example:

  • What is the number just before 5?
  • What is the number between 7 and 9?
  • Add one to 2. What is the result?
  • Minus two from 5. What is the result?

Features

  • Protects WordPress login, registration, password recovery and comment forms
  • Intelligent number-based challenges (0–9)
  • IP-based rate limiting
  • WordPress nonces and short-lived challenge tokens
  • Time-based validation
  • Honeypot field
  • Browser / automation detection signals
  • Colorblind-safe and high-contrast themes
  • Screen-reader friendly markup
  • Fully self-hosted – no external API calls
  • Clean uninstall removes all plugin options and data
  • No license keys, trials, quotas, or feature locks

All listed features are available on activation with no restrictions.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the rudyq-shield folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install the zip via Plugins → Add New → Upload.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings → RudyQ Shield to enable protection on the forms you want and choose theme / palette.
sections.faq:
Does it call any external service?

No. Everything runs on your server. No phone-home, no third-party APIs, no analytics beacons.

Are any features locked or license-gated?

No. The plugin is fully functional under the GPL. There are no license keys, trial periods, usage quotas, or disabled modules.

Can I remove the “Protected by RudyQ Shield” link?

The plugin shows a small credit link by default. Removing or changing it does not disable CAPTCHA, login, or any other feature. There is no attribution integrity lock.
